newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Ill. nukes to boost output in Sept.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Ill. nukes to boost output in Sept.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co (ComEd) has scheduled to restart or increase power from several of its nuclear power plants in Illinois in September, a company spokesman said.

ComEd's 794 megawatt (MW) Dresden unit 3, located at Morris, Ill., was expected to resume production this weekend or early next week after a shutdown which began June 30, company spokesman Gary Wald said.
The unit was shut for inspection and a fire protection system upgrade.
The company's Dresden unit 2, also at Morris, was operating near 90 percent of capacity and expected to hold at that level for several days for feedwater testing, Wald said.
The 1,040 MW Zion nuclear unit 1 at Zion, Ill., was also expected to boost output from its current 25 percent level later this week.
At the same time, the adjacent 1,040 MW Zion 2 unit was expected to shut down September 19 for about 58 days of scheduled maintenance, he said.
Also expected to shut down this month for scheduled maintenance is the 1,078 MW LaSalle unit 2, which Wald said will likely cease operations for an expected 65 days beginning September 20.
ComEd operates 12 nuclear power units in Illinois with a total capacity of 11,487 MW.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
